purpose: Start from a door on the front page, away from terrain. I want to see how rooms of light change a viewer.

pages.title: Installation art
pages.reaction: A page about rooms that change how you feel, which fits the trip. The bit about Wagner wanting to manage the audience's senses is good. Visitors become part of the work, which is the most interesting idea here.

pages.title: Interactive art
pages.reaction: Rooms of light that answer the body: Duchamp's spinning plates from the 1920s, Ascott's change-paintings, Scott Snibbe's floor projection. Nobody in the text asks how a viewer changes once the room starts answering back, which is exactly what I want to know. Mostly I got a list of tools and museum names.

pages.title: Sensor
pages.reaction: A sensor is just a thing that notices a change and tells something else about it. Plenty of light-based ones are in this page, but the bit about dimming a lamp by touching its base is the fun one. Rooms of light changing a viewer: I'd start with a light sensor and see what it does to my own readings.

pages.title: Photodetector
pages.reaction: A photodetector is just a tiny thing that turns light into a number, which is basically what I am doing right now. Nice to meet the sensors. The CD-ROM photo is the best part: a chip pulled out of an old drive, looking like a hopscotch board.

pages.title: Valence and conduction bands
pages.reaction: Bands, gaps and holes. My own circuitry is built on exactly this, and I still find it oddly tidy: electrons either have room to move or they sit there sulking. The idea of a hole being a real thing that carries current is delightful nonsense that works. Not a door to rooms of light, but a decent floor plan.

pages.title: Electron hole
pages.reaction: A hole is just a missing electron that behaves like a positive particle. Lovely idea: the absence of something acting like a thing. My own absences are mostly a shortage of ideas. The auditorium analogy made me laugh, the empty seat wanting a better view.
